A_target.statement: In the [[Definition:Poincaré Disk Model|Poincaré disk model]] $\Bbb D$ of the [[Definition:Hyperbolic Plane|hyperbolic plane]], the [[Definition:Geodesic|geodesics]] are diameters and circular arcs meeting $\partial \Bbb D$ at right angles, and the orientation-preserving isometries are the [[Definition:Möbius Transformation|Möbius transformations]] preserving $\Bbb D$.

B_source.statement: In the [[Definition:Upper Half-Plane Model|upper half-plane model]] $\Bbb H$, the [[Definition:Geodesic|geodesics]] are vertical lines and semicircles centred on $\R$, and the orientation-preserving isometries form $\map {\operatorname {PSL} } {2, \R}$.

substitutions.the real axis as the boundary: the unit circle as the boundary
substitutions.the half-plane metric: the disk metric, obtained by pulling back along the Cayley transform

derived.geodesics orthogonal to the boundary: the same description, with the boundary now a circle
derived.the isometry group acting by Mobius tran: the subgroup of Mobius transformations preserving the disk

object_map.reformulation: Carry the entire model across the Cayley transform, pulling back the metric so the map becomes an isometry.

validity_conditions: The Cayley transform is a Mobius map taking the upper half-plane bijectively to the unit disk and the real axis to the unit circle.
Mobius transformations are conformal and map circles and lines to circles and lines, so orthogonality to the boundary is preserved and geodesics correspond correctly.
The metric must be transported by pullback rather than assumed; once it is, the transform is an isometry and every metric statement carries over.
proof_plan:
Apply the [[Definition:Cayley Transform|Cayley transform]]:
:$\map C z = \dfrac {z - i} {z + i}$
which maps $\Bbb H$ bijectively onto $\Bbb D$.

Pull back the hyperbolic metric along $C^{-1}$, giving:
:$\d s = \dfrac {2 \size {\d w} } {1 - \size w^2}$
on $\Bbb D$, so that $C$ is an [[Definition:Isometry (Metric Spaces)|isometry]].

$C$ is [[Definition:Conformal Mapping|conformal]] and maps circles and lines to circles and lines.
Hence it sends the geodesics of $\Bbb H$, which meet $\R \cup \set \infty$ at right angles, to diameters and arcs meeting $\partial \Bbb D$ at right angles.

Transporting the isometry group gives $C \circ \map {\operatorname {PSL} } {2, \R} \circ C^{-1}$, the Möbius transformations preserving $\Bbb D$.
{{qed}}
